paragraphs.text: Bridge the HTTP Retry-After header into DeepSeek Harness retry policy on OpenAI-compatible (pi-ai) r
outes — 429 backoff made honest
# dsh-retry-after
**Stop guessing the backoff: let the provider tell you how long to wait.**

A plugin for DeepSeek Harness that bridges the HTTP
`Retry-After` header into the harness retry poli
cy — on the routes where it is currently thrown away.
中文说明 · Design notes
## The problem
When a gateway answers `429 Too Many Requests`, it usually says when to come back:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The harness already knows how to honour that: `LlmFailure.providerRetryAfterMs` exists exactly for i

t,
`dsh-llm-retry` reads it, and the native DeepSeek transport fills it in from the response headers

,
`dsh-llm-retry` reads it, and the native DeepSeek transport fills it in from the response headers.
Every OpenAI-compatible route (the `llm-pi-ai` plugin, which covers OpenCode, OpenRouter, vLLM, Lite

LLM
and friends) loses it on the way:
1. `@earendil-works/pi-ai` catches the provider error and rethrows `new Error(...)` — status and hea

ders gone.
2. `dsh-llm-pi-ai` classifies that string with `classifyPiAiError`, which pattern-matches

the message text.
3. `dsh-llm-retry` gets a failure with no timing hint, so it falls back to its ow

n backoff:
`initialDelayMs` (500 ms by default), doubling, jittered.
So a gateway that asks for **20 seconds** gets hit again after **500 milliseconds**. Retries burn do

uble,
and a soft rate limit turns into a hard one.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What this plugin does
It reads the headers *before* they are dropped — at the `fetch` edge — and writes them back onto the
failure object, in the one slot `dsh-llm-retry` already reads.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Concretely, on every `agent/request-error` it:
| Fact | Added as | Why |

| response status | `failure.status` | diagnostics; keeps the record honest |
| `Retry-After` (or `R

etry-After-Ms`) | `failure.providerRetryAfterMs` | the delay the provider asked for |
| corrected er
ror code | `failure.code` | a localized 429 body ("请求过于频繁") classifies as `PI_AI_ERROR` and never en
ters the retry list; the captured **status** does not care what language the gateway writes in |

Nothing else changes. The retry budget, jitter, cancellation, `llm/retry` events and per-provider
`r
etryPolicy` all stay with `dsh-llm-retry`. This is a translator, not a second retry loop.
## Measured effect

A mock gateway that answers `429` with `retry-after: 2` three times, then succeeds
(`test/mock-gatew
ay.mjs`, `test/mock.patch.yml`):
| | attempt gap #1→#2 | #2→#3 |

| without the plugin | 500 ms | 1000 ms (local backoff) |
| with the plugin | **2030 ms** | **2030 m
s** (what the gateway asked for) |

## Configuration
Everything is optional; the defaults are what you want almost always. The row lives in your profile'

s
`cordis.patch.yml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### `oversize`
`dsh-llm-retry` gives up instead of retrying when the requested delay exceeds `retryPolicy.maxDelayM

s`
(in `normal` mode). That is a reasonable default — the provider just told you it is busy for an h

our —
but it can also kill a turn that would have recovered after a slightly longer wait.
- `clamp` *(default)* — wait `maxDelayMs`, keep retrying. Never wait longer than your policy allows.
- `honor` — pass the provider's number through. An oversized hint ends the retry, as designed upstr

eam.
- `ignore` — drop the hint, use local backoff. Useful when the gateway's numbers are nonsense.
### `floorMsByCode`

Risk-control gateways sometimes answer 429 with **no** `Retry-After` at all. A floor gives those a
m
inimum wait, so local backoff cannot hammer them:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Limitations
Read these before relying on it.
- **Correlation is a heuristic.** `pi-ai` hands the harness no request id, so a failure is matched t

o a
capture by **origin** (scheme + host + port) and **recency** (`windowMs`). Two providers sharing

one
origin, failing within the window, can be attributed to each other. With one provider per origi

n —
the normal case — this is exact.
- **Concurrency.** Parallel subagent requests to the same origi

n share the ring buffer; the newest
record wins. A 429 for one request may annotate another. The del

ay is still a real number from that
origin, so the cost is a suboptimal wait, not a wrong retry.
- *

*The failure object is frozen.** This was a surprise during development: `Object.isExtensible` is
fa
lse on the failure the agent loop hands to the waterfall, so writes throw. The plugin clones it and
replaces `payload.failure`, which works because `dsh-llm-retry` destructures the payload *after* thi

s
prepended listener runs. If a future harness freezes the payload too, the plugin degrades to doing

nothing (and says so in `debug`).
- **Fetch-based transports only.** Routes using the WebSocket tra

nsport never produce an HTTP response
to observe; they are untouched (they also carry their own erro

r handling).
- **It does not reduce burst.** Honouring `Retry-After` makes each retry wait longer; i

t does not stop
the request that caused the 429. Pair it with sane prompt/context sizes if you are h

itting hard
limits repeatedly.
- **Native routes do not need it.** `deepseek-official` already fills

`providerRetryAfterMs`; the plugin
is a no-op there (it finds no capture and leaves the failure alo

oviderRetryAfterMs`; the plugin
is a no-op there (it finds no capture and leaves the failure alone).
## When to use something else

- You want more retries with a different policy → `dsh-retry-boost`
- You want to fail over to anoth

er model or provider → `dsh-llm-fallbacks`
- You want the transport fixed upstream → `@earendil-work
s/pi-ai` #9595, #8507 (both declined); the harness-side ask is discussion #8992
